correctness.rationale: For three angularly uniform circle points the half-gap angle triple is Dirichlet(1,1,1), with A,B density 2/pi^2. The signed orthic identity Q=2|cos A cos B cos C| correctly includes obtuse triangles. Product-to-sum gives E[cos A cos B cos C]=-1/4; the acute conditional simplex yields E[P 1acute]=3/(4pi^2)-1/16, and hence E Q=1/4+3/pi^2. Each small-ratio corner has local product Q=2|y(x+y)|(1+O(x^2+y^2)) in the wedge x>=0; same-sign wedges and an opposite-sign quadrant give t log(1/t)+O(t) angle area, times three corners and density 2/pi^2. Each near-flat corner has Q=2-2(u^2+uv+v^2)+O((u+v)^4) and area pi*t/(6sqrt3); summing three gives the upper slope 1/(pi sqrt3). Independent 700000-sample exponential-simplex numerical diagnostic gave mean 0.55453 versus 0.55396 and upper-tail ratios near 1; lower-tail ratios remained >1 due to a non-negligible O(t) correction, not interpreted as limit proof.
